body.statement: At \(d=1\), \(m=6\), \(s=4\), and \(\alpha=\beta=27/200\), the interaction envelope gives \(R_n\gtrsim n^{-243/697}\); moreover \(243/697<27/77<5/14\), so this legal subfamily is slower than both the scalar smooth-functional benchmark \(n^{-27/77}\) and the oracle \(W_1\) benchmark \(n^{-5/14}\).
body.justification: A concrete strict exponent separation prevents the proposal from collapsing to a generic maximum of two published rates.
body.gap: RobinsEtAl2017HOIF supplies the scalar exponent and NilesWeedBerthet2022 supplies the oracle exponent, but neither likelihood construction contains the shared propensity across a multivariate outcome packing.
body.consumer: This tuple is an early known-design benchmark for testing finite-order correction code before solving the full asymmetric phase diagram.
